prompt: Solve for $x$: $\frac{x}{3} - 2 = 4$. Give just the number.
hint: The $-2$ happened last, so undo it first: add $2$ to both sides.

hints.text: The $-2$ happened last, so undo it first: add $2$ to both sides.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Simpler version: $\frac{x}{3} = 4$ gives $x = 12$. Your problem just has a $-2$ to undo FIRST, before you multiply by $3$.
$\frac{x}{3} = 6$. Now undo the "divide by 3" by multiplying both sides by $3$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Unwrap the present
steps: $x$ got wrapped twice: first "divide by 3", then "minus 2".
Unwrap in reverse: add 2 back (get 6), then multiply by 3 (get 18).

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ Dodge the trap
steps: Multiplying by 3 first gives x − 2 = 12 — but the −2 was never divided by 3, so that move breaks the equation.
Unwrap backwards: the last thing done to x was −2, so undo it first (x/3 = 6), THEN multiply by 3 to get 18.
